hypothesis: Among the three measured native high-quality teacher local hypotheses under identical scalar controller settings (parent L109, R11, half=1.0, endpoint/orientation/type=0.0, cat_noise_level=1.0, coord_noise_level=0.2, native_rms_ratio=0.66, max_atom_step_A=0.15, max_cumulative_rms_A=6.0, pointcloud_delta_A=1.0), Q017_20 (F_b017_s021_native, N@8/C@20) has the strongest supported local role/neighborhood compatibility for a lineage-aware guidance hypothesis. Its typed N slot 8 is a native acceptor aromatic degree-two pyridine-type N (native_to_desired N->N) with the highest teacher_match_strength among the three anchors (0.8545 vs 0.8438 for Q004_20 and 0.8255 for Q007_20), and its typed C slot 20 is a native aromatic CH (C->C) whose best_donor_strength is essentially zero (1.79e-06), i.e. no donor competition at the C site. Q004_20's N@6 anchor is slightly weaker (0.8438) and its C@8 site carries a nonzero donor strength (0.0703), while Q007_20's N@12 anchor is weakest (0.8255) and its C@8 site is near a donor (A:ASN:118:N, strength 9.6e-12, effectively zero but with a different donor residue). The joint layout contrast therefore separates the three on supported role/neighborhood compatibility, with Q017_20 the most discriminating native layout to test next.
